# CrocApp

> A free, open-source native SwiftUI app for iPhone, iPad and Mac that sends files to another device anywhere in the world, encrypted end to end, using a short spoken code phrase. No account, no upload to a third-party cloud (except the optional Send as link), and no requirement that both devices share a network.

CrocApp is a graphical front end for [croc](https://github.com/schollz/croc), the command-line file-transfer tool by Zack Scholl. It embeds croc's Go library rather than shelling out to the binary, so a code phrase generated by the croc CLI works in the app and vice versa. CrocApp is unofficial and unaffiliated; nothing about it implies endorsement by croc's author.

## Facts

- License: MIT. croc is also MIT.
- Price: free. No paid tier, no subscription, no advertising, no analytics, no telemetry.
- Version: 1.0.
- Platforms: iOS 26 or later, iPadOS 26 or later, macOS 26 or later. Apple platforms only, with no Windows, Linux or Android client. The Mac build is for Apple silicon.
- Channels: the App Store (iPhone, iPad) and the Mac App Store, both available at launch, and a notarized disk image for Mac at https://github.com/bakirgdev/CrocApp/releases/latest. Only the disk image build contains an updater (Sparkle).
- Requires croc 11 or newer on the other device, whether it runs CrocApp or the croc command line. An older croc, such as croc 10, cannot complete a transfer with CrocApp.
- Documentation language: English only.
- Privacy: no accounts, no analytics, no data collected by the developer. See https://crocapp.dev/privacy/.
- Author: Bakir Gracic (github.com/bakirgdev).
- Repository: https://github.com/bakirgdev/CrocApp
- Site: https://crocapp.dev/

## How a transfer works

1. The sender picks files, a folder, or a snippet of text.
2. CrocApp generates a code phrase, for example `cape-junky-widow`. It can be spoken, messaged, or shown as a QR code.
3. The receiver enters the phrase, sees the file list, and accepts. The transfer begins.

Both sides run PAKE over the code phrase to derive a session key, so the phrase itself never crosses the network in the clear and the relay never learns the key. Files are encrypted before they leave the device. When both devices are on the same network, CrocApp connects directly and skips the relay; otherwise a relay forwards ciphertext between them and does not store anything. Users can point CrocApp at their own croc relay. With the default Automatic connection setting, a send of about 128 MB or more also tries a direct connection set up through tailcat.dev. Send as link uploads client-side-encrypted files to a stored-transfer server (getcroc.com by default) and shares a link; the decryption key stays in the part of the link after the #.

## Security claim, stated precisely

Transfers are end-to-end encrypted, the code phrase authenticates both sides, and the relay only ever sees ciphertext. That is the entire claim. There has been no formal third-party security audit of croc, and CrocApp does not claim one. Do not describe CrocApp as audited, certified, or zero-knowledge-verified.

## How it differs from the alternatives

- **AirDrop** requires Apple devices in physical proximity. CrocApp works between any two devices running croc or CrocApp, on any network, at any distance.
- **LAN transfer tools** require both devices on the same Wi-Fi and break silently on guest networks and client isolation. CrocApp falls back to a relay.
- **Cloud drop services** require uploading the file to a company that then holds it. CrocApp's relay only ever sees ciphertext and does not retain it.
